questions.question: You approach an intersection during the day and need to turn around. Based on the combination sign provided, what are you legally allowed to do?

options.text: You cannot execute a U-turn at any time of the day or night.
You are prohibited from making a U-turn only during night-time hours.
You must make a U-turn immediately to clear the intersection before nightfall.
You are prohibited from turning right, but a U-turn is permitted during the day.

questions.explanation: The night-time supplementary plate (stars and moon) limits the no-U-turn prohibition to night-time hours, so a U-turn is allowed during the day.

questions.question: A driver stops a vehicle on a public road because they are waiting for a friend who is running late. The vehicle remains stationary for several minutes. How is this situation most accurately classified?

options.text: Parking
Standing
Stopping
Loading

questions.explanation: Keeping a vehicle stationary for longer than needed to load/offload or pick up/drop passengers (e.g. waiting for a friend) counts as parking.

questions.question: You are driving a standard private motor car and approach a road displaying the sign provided. The current time is 08:00 AM on a Tuesday. Are you legally allowed to enter this road?

options.text: Yes, because private motor cars are always considered authorized vehicles on public roads.
No, unauthorized vehicles are strictly prohibited from entering this road during the two specific time periods shown.
Yes, you can enter at any time, but you are not allowed to park or stop on this road during those hours.
No, this road is permanently closed to all traffic except emergency vehicles.

questions.explanation: The no-entry-for-unauthorised-vehicles sign applies during the times shown (06:30–09:00 and 16:00–20:00), so you may not enter at 08:00.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the use of a cellphone while driving is correct?

options.text: It may be held in one hand if the vehicle is travelling below 40 km/h
It may be used while stopped at a red traffic light
It may not be held while driving unless it is secured in a fixed mounting
It may be used if the driver keeps both eyes on the road

questions.explanation: A cellphone may not be held in the hand while driving; it may only be used hands-free / in a fixed mounting.

questions.question: You are driving on a freeway and see the combination sign provided. What is the legal requirement of this sign?

options.text: You are approaching a public transit terminal where only taxis and buses are allowed to enter.
You are on a toll road and are legally required to pay a toll at the collection point located 400 meters ahead.
You must maintain a minimum speed of 40 km/h for the next 400 meters of the roadway.
You are entering a telephone-only emergency zone that lasts for a distance of 400 meters.

questions.explanation: The blue 'T' command sign indicates a toll route: you must pay toll at the toll plaza, here 400 m ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on a freeway and miss your intended off-ramp. What is the correct action?

options.text: Reverse carefully along the shoulder to the off-ramp
Stop on the shoulder and wait for a gap in traffic
Make a U-turn when traffic allows
Continue to the next off-ramp and leave the freeway there

questions.explanation: Never reverse, stop or U-turn on a freeway; continue to the next off-ramp.

questions.question: You are driving on a road and encounter this temporary warning sign. What does this sign require you to do?

options.text: Expect a steep side-slope on the road surface and accelerate to maintain traction.
Be alert for an upcoming vehicle towing zone or salvage yard entrance.
Slow down immediately and prepare for an accident scene ahead that may block the roadway.
Watch out for high-sided delivery trucks that are at risk of overturning due to high winds.

questions.explanation: Yellow temporary sign warning of a crashed/overturned vehicle (accident scene) ahead: reduce speed and be prepared for sudden traffic. (Answer from the video's explanation; no letter was read out.)

questions.question: Which of the following vehicles may legally use a freeway?

options.text: A motorcycle with an engine capacity of 40 cc
A vehicle being towed by a rope
A motor vehicle capable of maintaining an appropriate freeway speed
An animal-drawn vehicle travelling on the shoulder

questions.explanation: Slow vehicles such as animal-drawn vehicles, very low-powered motorcycles and vehicles towed by a rope may not use a freeway; only vehicles able to keep up with freeway speeds safely may. (Answer from the video's explanation.)

questions.question: You are driving on a rural road and see this temporary warning sign. What does this sign indicate?

options.text: A temporary manual stop/go control point is ahead, where you must prepare to stop and wait for a signal to proceed.
A pedestrians-only walkway begins ahead, and all motor vehicles must detour.
A permanent scholar patrol zone is located directly around the next corner.
A law enforcement checkpoint is active ahead for vehicle roadworthy inspections.

questions.explanation: Temporary 'stop/go control ahead' warning sign: road works with traffic reduced to one lane; slow down and be ready to stop when a flagman signals.

questions.question: A vehicle is being towed on a public road. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The towing connection may exceed 3.5 metres if a warning flag is attached
The towing connection may not exceed 3.5 metres in length
There is no maximum length provided both drivers are licensed
A chain may only be used at night

questions.explanation: The distance between a towing and a towed vehicle (tow rope/chain/bar) may not exceed 3.5 m.
